steps.title: Welcome!
steps.purpose: Greet the child and set emotional tone
steps.owlText: Hello friend! Today we are going to learn about two special fractions: one half and one quarter. Are you ready?
steps.studentText: Today we learn about one half (1/2) and one quarter (1/4)!

media.altText: Owl teacher waving hello with two shapes: one showing 1/2 and one showing 1/4
media.fallbackText: Owl teacher waving hello with two shapes: one showing 1/2 and one showing 1/4

steps.title: Our Mission
steps.purpose: Tell the child what they will learn
steps.studentText: Today you will learn to tell the difference between one half (1/2) and one quarter (1/4). Both are fractions, but they are different!

steps.title: Think First!
steps.purpose: Activate prior knowledge about halves and quarters
steps.owlText: Before we start, think about this: If you cut a chapati into 2 equal pieces, and your friend cuts the same size chapati into 4 equal pieces, which piece is bigger — your piece or your friend's piece?
steps.studentText: Think about it: Is a half bigger or smaller than a quarter? Draw or describe your thinking.

media.altText: Two chapatis side by side: one cut into 2 pieces, one cut into 4 pieces, with a question mark
media.fallbackText: Two chapatis side by side: one cut into 2 pieces, one cut into 4 pieces, with a question mark

interaction.question: Is one half (1/2) bigger or smaller than one quarter (1/4)? Why do you think so?

steps.title: Learn It
steps.purpose: Teach the difference between 1/2 and 1/4 visually
steps.owlText: Let me show you. Here are two same-size rectangles. The first is divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded — that is one half (1/2). The second is divided into 4 equal parts. One part is shaded — that is one quarter (1/4). Look at the shaded parts. The half is bigger! Both are fractions, but they are different.
steps.studentText: One half (1/2) and one quarter (1/4) are both fractions. When the wholes are the same size, one half is bigger than one quarter. The more parts you make, the smaller each part becomes.

media.altText: Two same-size rectangles side by side. Left: divided into 2 equal parts, 1 shaded (1/2). Right: divided into 4 equal parts, 1 shaded (1/4). The 1/2 shaded area is visibly larger.
media.caption: One half (1/2) and one quarter (1/4). The half is bigger.
media.fallbackText: Two same-size rectangles side by side. Left: divided into 2 equal parts, 1 shaded (1/2). Right: divided into 4 equal parts, 1 shaded (1/4). The 1/2 shaded area is visibly larger.

steps.title: Real Life Connection
steps.purpose: Connect comparing fractions to real life
steps.owlText: We see this in real life! If you share a pizza with one friend (2 people), you get a bigger slice than if you share with 3 friends (4 people). More people means smaller pieces. The same chapati cut into 2 gives bigger pieces than cut into 4!
steps.studentText: When you share with more people, each person gets a smaller piece. A half is bigger than a quarter because there are fewer parts.

media.altText: Two pizzas: one cut into 2 big slices, one cut into 4 small slices. People sharing.
media.fallbackText: Two pizzas: one cut into 2 big slices, one cut into 4 small slices. People sharing.

steps.title: Watch and Learn
steps.purpose: Show worked examples of identifying 1/2 vs 1/4
steps.owlText: Let me show you how to tell them apart. This shape is divided into 2 equal parts. One is shaded. That is one half (1/2). This shape is divided into 4 equal parts. One is shaded. That is one quarter (1/4). Count the total parts to know which fraction it is!
steps.studentText: To tell fractions apart: Count the total number of equal parts. 2 parts total = one half. 4 parts total = one quarter. One shaded part in both cases.

media.altText: Two shapes: one labeled 1/2 (2 parts, 1 shaded), one labeled 1/4 (4 parts, 1 shaded). Counting arrows show total parts.
media.fallbackText: Two shapes: one labeled 1/2 (2 parts, 1 shaded), one labeled 1/4 (4 parts, 1 shaded). Counting arrows show total parts.

steps.title: Your Turn!
steps.purpose: Practice identifying whether a shape shows 1/2 or 1/4
steps.owlText: Now it is your turn! Look at this shape. Is it showing one half (1/2) or one quarter (1/4)? Tap the correct answer.
steps.studentText: This shape has one part shaded. How many equal parts is the whole divided into? Is it 1/2 or 1/4?

media.altText: A rectangle divided into 4 equal parts with 1 part shaded.
media.fallbackText: A rectangle divided into 4 equal parts with 1 part shaded.

interaction.question: What fraction is shaded?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! The shape is divided into 4 equal parts and 1 is shaded. That is one quarter (1/4)!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Count the total equal parts. There are 4. One is shaded. That is one quarter (1/4).

steps.title: Quick Check!
steps.purpose: Test understanding of equal vs unequal parts (QC-E1)
steps.owlText: Quick check! Which shape shows equal parts? Remember: fractions need parts that are the same size.

media.altText: Four shapes: A has 2 equal parts, B has 2 unequal parts, C has 3 unequal parts, D has 4 unequal parts.
media.fallbackText: Four shapes: A has 2 equal parts, B has 2 unequal parts, C has 3 unequal parts, D has 4 unequal parts.

interaction.question: Which shape shows equal parts?
options: Shape A: rectangle divided into 2 equal parts
Shape B: rectangle divided into 2 unequal parts
Shape C: circle divided into 3 unequal parts
Shape D: square divided into 4 unequal parts
interaction.correctAnswer: Shape A: rectangle divided into 2 equal parts
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! Only Shape A has equal parts. Fractions need equal parts!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Remember: fractions need parts that are the same size. Look for the shape where all parts are equal.

steps.title: Think About Your Learning
steps.owlText: You did great today! Think about what you learned. What is the difference between one half and one quarter? Both are fractions, but they are different!
steps.studentText: What did you learn about one half (1/2) and one quarter (1/4) today?

interaction.question: How do you feel about halves and quarters today?

steps.title: You Did It!
steps.owlText: Wonderful! You learned about one half (1/2) and one quarter (1/4) today. Remember: count the equal parts to know the fraction. Keep practicing!
steps.studentText: You learned about halves and quarters! Count the equal parts to tell them apart!

media.altText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I know 1/2 and 1/4!'
media.fallbackText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I know 1/2 and 1/4!'
